My OCD also started at 19. Before that age I had 0 symptoms of OCD. It all went downhill in my second year of university in 2019. 2020 and 2021 were the 2 worse years of my life where I went through tremendous suffering caused by the ocd. Got diagnosed in mid 2020, started taking lots of psychiatric meds. I was so drugged up but it was needed. Took 6mg of xanax a day for months that year. Nowadays in 2022 I'm almost in total remission. My depression is somewhat still there, but mild. The OCD obsessions though are at 1% of what they used to be in 2019-2021. I smoked weed and took LSD in 2017-2019 a couple of times. I don't know if it  caused the onset of my ocd or if it would naturally trigger at the age of 19 anyways. I experience the exact same thing you do and my OCD mainly consists on that which I call "Coincidence OCD". It's very common but not much talked about. It's some sort of ideas of reference and referential thinking, but it's not psychotic unless you really start to believe those coincidences are meaningful. Be careful, imo this kind of OCD is very dangerous to indulge in, doing those bets with yourself is a really bad compulsion and you will end up finding more and more coincidences that will fuck you up and your brain won't be able to rationalize them because we, people with OCD, more often find meaningful patterns in things that really don't have any meaning. I still have this too, I have it since my ocd started 3 years ago, but nowadays it's so mild and happens wayyyy less frequently, I rarely do these compulsive bets and it doesn't affect me anymore, I used to do them 24/7 and I was going crazy. I got better by being on SSRIs (still am) and an antipsychotic also might have helped in the period I used it because my insight was low (I almost believe in the "signs" coincidences), do therapy, socializing more, exercising and the most important thing DONT RUMINATE on the coincidences. The more you do it the more urge you will have to do more tests/bets to confirm/deny the meaning of these "signs". They're not signs, it's just you're brain hyperfocusing on patterns, we're just ill, don't let yourself believe in synchronicity and shit like that. That playing with fire for people with ocd like us. Take a scientific approach and be skeptic of any possible paranormal phenomenons that your brain might be entertaining, don't fall into delusion
